content.text:
The drawing shows a 1H-indazole ring system with an NH substituent at position 4 and a wavy line on the NH, marking the attachment point.

Indazole numbering: N1(H), N2, C3, C3a, C4, C5, C6, C7, C7a. In the image, the five-membered ring has N (top) double-bonded to CH, and NH attached to the benzo ring at the upper right. The CH (C3) joins C3a, which sits at the ring fusion. The NH–aryl carbon is directly below C3a, so it is C4.

SMILES: the fragment is *Nc1cccc2[nH]ncc12

Check: c1 (C4) bears the NH, followed by c (C5), c (C6), c (C7), c2 (C7a), [nH] (N1), n (N2), c (C3), and c12 (C3a) closes both rings. C3a bonds to C4 through ring closure 1 and to C7a through ring closure 2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: *Nc1cccc2[nH]ncc12
